statements.text: Assessment: right lumbar radiculopathy at L5-S1 due to disc herniation with foraminal stenosis.
MRI lumbar spine 08/24/2026: L5-S1 disc herniation with moderate right foraminal stenosis contacting the exiting nerve root.
Function: unable to stand long enough to cook a meal, has stopped driving because of the pain.
Baseline NRS prior to any intervention: 9/10.
Reports low back pain radiating to the right leg for 22 weeks.
Completed physical therapy from 04/16/2026 to 05/14/2026 (4 weeks) with no lasting benefit, and failed ibuprofen 600 mg TID.
Continues the daily home exercise program taught in PT.
No red flags: afebrile, no unexplained weight loss, no history of malignancy, no saddle anesthesia.
Epidural steroid injection history: 2 lumbar injections in the past 12 months (10/16/2025, 01/02/2026).

Subjective:
Adrian presented with ongoing symptoms despite conservative management. He reported persistent discomfort affecting daily activities.

Objective:
Throughout the therapy period, assessments indicated limited improvement in range of motion and functional capacity.

The patient underwent a structured physical therapy program focusing on mobility and strengthening exercises.

Outcome:
